_about: Probes: realistic sentences where a lexicon word appears in another sense (an agency, a card, a job, a body part, a charity), each paired with the true positive it must not break. Started from an outside finding ("I don't have a social security number" flagged a mother as a senior). Scored with the rest; failures here were fixed by tightening the lexicon, never by editing the case.

cases.text: I'm a mother of three kids aged 2, 5 and 8 and we need food. I don't have a social security number.
cases._why: outside review: SSN sentence flagged a 30-something mother as a senior and flipped two 60+ programs to likely

cases.text: I lost my social security card and need food for my kids
cases._why: a card is not an age

cases.text: The social security office cut my kids' survivor benefits and now we can't buy groceries
cases._why: survivor benefits go to children

cases.text: My son gets SSDI from Social Security and we're behind on rent

cases.text: Social Security cut my SSI and I can't pay rent
